. Centripetal force is defined as any net force causing uniform circular motion. The centripetal force is not a
new kind of force. The label “centripetal” refers to any force that keeps something turning in a circle. That
force could be tension, gravity, friction, electrical attraction, the normal force, or any other force. Any
combination of these could be the source of centripetal force, for example, the centripetal force at the top of
the path of a tetherball swung through a vertical circle is the result of both tension and gravity.
